lede: The biggest thing on the calendar this week is Monday's Town Council meeting, where a vote on converting two units at 215 East Colorado Avenue from price-capped affordable ownership to employee dwelling units will effectively rewrite how those homes function in Telluride's housing stock — and that same deed-restriction question carries through a Housing Authority meeting and public hearings on the same day. The County Commissioners also have a continued public hearing Tuesday on adopting new international building codes and a low-carbon energy code that will shape what gets built here for years to come. Elsewhere, P&Z gets an early look at a proposed employee housing project at the middle-high school site, and the School Board moves to formal votes on two state ballot measures and updated board policies.

notable.stake: Vote to strip price caps from two affordable units, changing them to EDUs.
